# Compiler errors the native half is allowed to produce. THE BASELINE IS EMPTY.
#
# Empty means the native job is a plain build gate: every target and every test target must compile
# cleanly on every run, and any compile error at all fails the job on the first run that introduces
# it. Nothing in src/native is exempt.
#
# It was NOT empty when this file arrived. The first CI runs on this repository discovered that main
# did not compile at all — 2 C errors in Updater/VerifierLauncher and 4 Swift errors in
# Updater/Protocol, measured on macos-latest (macOS 26.4, Apple Swift 6.3.2, Xcode 26.5,
# SDK MacOSX26.5.sdk) in runs 30302342895 and 30305062756. Between them they blocked
# RecordingsVerifierLauncher, RecordingsUpdateBroker, RecordingsUpdateBrokerTests,
# RecordingsUpdateProtocol, RecordingsUpdateClient, RecordingsEnvelopeSigner,
# RecordingsBootstrapPreflight and RecordingsUpdateProtocolTests — 31 of the 84 Swift files that
# belonged to a target, i.e. the entire updater subsystem, about 37% of the Swift.
#
# They were fixed in #55, which is what emptied this file: `swift build --build-tests` and
# `swift test` both exit 0 on the merged tree, all five executable products link, and every one of
# the eight targets above appears in a `Compiling` line. The six entries were removed in the same
# change, because scripts/ci-native-build.ts fails the job when a blocked target starts building
# cleanly — this file cannot outlive the defects it describes, in either direction.
#
# WHAT AN EMPTY BASELINE DOES NOT CLAIM: that the native half is verified. It says the native half
# COMPILES. The runtime behaviour of the Swift test targets is TCC-gated (microphone, clipboard,
# accessibility) and `swift test` is deliberately not a gate on a headless runner — see the
# `native` job in ci.yml, which records that outcome rather than asserting one.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IF YOU ARE ABOUT TO ADD AN ENTRY, READ THIS FIRST.
#
# Adding one re-exempts every target that entry blocks, plus everything that depends on them, and the
# transitive closure is easy to underestimate: two C errors in one launcher file blocked eight
# targets. An entry here is not a note, it is a hole in the only regression protection the Swift/C
# half has.
#
# So: fix the error instead. If it genuinely cannot be fixed in the same change, then adding an entry
# also means deleting the "the baseline is empty" test in src/__tests__/ci-native-build.test.ts, in
# that same change, with the blast radius named in the PR body. That test exists to make re-exempting
# the native half a deliberate and reviewable act rather than a one-line append nobody notices.
#
# Format, if an entry is ever justified:
#   <repo-relative source file>: <clang/swift message, truncated at the first ';'>
# Line and column numbers are deliberately NOT part of the signature — they move whenever anything
# above them is edited, and a signature that churns is a signature nobody maintains. The cost of that
# choice, stated plainly: a SECOND occurrence of an already-listed message in the same file is not
# distinguishable from the first, so it would not be caught.
#
# Which targets an entry blocks is DERIVED, not configured: scripts/ci-native-build.ts maps each
# entry to its owning target via `swift package dump-package` and then closes over dependents. Do not
# hand-maintain a list of blocked targets here; read the job's output instead.
